clean.title: Turn Bay Transition - Single or Double Centerline
clean.summary: City of Pasadena standard plan S-702, revision 1, dual units, dated 6/4/01. It lays out a left turn bay transition from the centerline of the street with a 30:1 taper from point A over a 45 m (150 ft) length, and gives a six step procedure to mark points A through J and form the curves.
clean.notes:
Procedure to install transition:
1. Layout points A, D, G, & H.
2. Use points A & D to determine a straight line and mark B & C.
3. Use points C & G to determine a straight line and mark E & F.
4. Mark J by measuring 180 mm (7") in from C. Mark I by measuring 150 mm (6") in from G.
5. Form curves B-J-E & F-I-H.
6. Stripe.
clean.description:
Plan view of the transition: A horizontal street centerline is drawn as a dash-dot line. The transition starts at point A at the left (START OF TRANSITION) where the striping leaves the centerline on a 30:1 taper. The tapered line runs 27 m (90') to point B and the overall length to the end of transition is 45 m (150'). A smooth S curve then moves the line across the centerline to point H at the end of transition. Points B and C, E and F, I and J are used to form two curves, B-J-E and F-I-H. Along the baseline from B to the end of transition the segments are 3 m (10'), 3 m (10'), 6 m (20'), 3 m (10') and 3 m (10'). At the end of transition the lateral offsets are 1.5 m (5') from point D to the centerline and 3 m (10') between points D and H. Thick segments mark the striping lines at start and end. Dashed construction lines connect A to D and C to G, and points D, G and H are the layout points.

Procedure to install transition: see the numbered steps in the notes.

clean.title: Speed Humps and Speed Cushions
clean.summary: Pasadena standard for installing 3.5 inch asphalt speed humps and speed cushions, with installation notes, warning sign and temporary signing requirements. Separate sheets give hump layouts for streets under 50 ft wide and 50 ft or wider, and cushion layouts for streets 28 ft to 38 ft and 38 ft and greater. Humps are 12 ft long in the direction of travel with a 3.5 inch nominal height, built of Type D2 PG 64-10 asphalt, and marked with thermoplastic. A W17-1 SPEED HUMP sign and a flashing barricade with W8-1 or W17-1 and W13-1 signs are required until the pavement markings are in place.
clean.notes:
Installation details:
1. Speed humps shall not be placed over manholes, watergates, junction chambers, etc.
2. Edge of speed hump should be 10 ft minimum from edge and uphill of driveway.
3. Height of speed hump shall nominally be 3.5 in +/- 0.25 in at all cross sections.
4. Whenever possible, speed humps shall be placed at property lines instead of mid-lot.
5. Whenever possible, speed humps shall be placed adjacent to street lights.
6. Speed humps shall be marked using thermoplastic material.
7. Speed hump signs shall be installed per Figure A, where noted on plans.
Figure A: Speed hump warning sign (typical). Warning flags (first 30 days). 30 in x 30 in. Black on yellow or W17-1 SPEED HUMP, 6 in Series E letters. W13-1(15) sign. Sign locations: as directed by Engineer.
Temporary signage details:
1. The contractor shall furnish and maintain a flashing barricade, 50 feet from each speed hump location in both directions, until the first application of paint has been applied showing the pavement messages and striping.
2. Mount 30 in x 30 in W8-1 or W17-1 warning sign (black on yellow, 6 in Series E letters) and W13-1 sign per MUTCD with the California Supplement, on each of the barricades at each speed hump location.
clean.description:
Installation details box: A boxed list titled INSTALLATION DETAILS with seven numbered requirements for speed humps (see notes).

Figure A, speed hump warning sign (typical): A drawing of a diamond-shaped warning sign reading SPEED HUMP with a pair of warning flags mounted on its upper corners. Below it on the same post is a small rectangular plaque reading 15 MPH, labeled W13-1(15) SIGN. Callouts: WARNING FLAGS (FIRST 30-DAYS), 30in X 30in, BLACK ON YELLOW OR W17-1 "SPEED HUMP", 6 in SERIES E LETTERS, and SIGN LOCATIONS: AS DIRECTED BY ENGINEER.

Temporary signage details box: A boxed list titled TEMPORARY SIGNAGE DETAILS with two numbered requirements for flashing barricades and signs during construction.

clean.title: Crosswalk Installation
clean.summary: Pasadena standard layouts for marked crosswalks, covering the basic crosswalk, the zebra crosswalk and the continental crosswalk. All striping is 12 in white or yellow thermoplastic or similar material. Bar spacing starts from the street center line and avoids the wheel path, and bars are parallel to traffic flow at skewed or offset intersections. Continental bars are 2 ft wide and 14 ft long, and a 12 in white limit line is typically used only in advance of signalized intersections.
clean.notes:
Notes:
1. All striping shall be 12 in white or yellow, in thermoplastic or similar material.
2. White 12 in limit line in advance of crosswalks typically installed only in advance of signalized intersections, other locations and only when specified. In thermoplastic material or similar material.
Labels: Double yellow center line (DYCL). Approach to intersection. Leaving side of intersection. Curb face. Edge of gutter. B.C. E.C. Angle phi and phi/2. Dimensions: 4 ft (limit line to crosswalk line), 12 ft (between the two crosswalk lines), 4 ft (at the corner diagonal).
clean.description:
Plan view, basic crosswalk (sheet 1 of 3): A corner of an intersection is drawn with a curb return running from B.C. (beginning of curve) to E.C. (end of curve). The central angle is labeled phi, split by a bisecting radial line into two angles labeled phi/2. The curb face is shown as a heavy solid line with the edge of gutter as a dashed line outside it. The approach to the intersection runs along the top left, with the DOUBLE YELLOW CENTER LINE (DYCL) drawn as two yellow lines. The leaving side of the intersection runs down the right side, also with a DYCL. The crosswalk is formed by two heavy parallel lines, 12' apart, across each leg. The two lines turn through a 45 degree chamfer at the corner so that the crosswalk is one continuous L-shaped path around the curb return. A gray limit line (callout 2) runs from the DYCL to the curb face on the approach, 4' back from the near crosswalk line. A second 4' dimension is shown at the corner diagonal. The crosswalk lines on the approach leg and on the leaving leg are each marked with callout 1.

clean.title: Raised Pavement Marker Installation Detail
clean.summary: Pasadena detail for placing raised pavement markers (RPMs) with different stripe types. Twelve details cover two-way no passing zones, painted medians, left and right turn lane stripes, lane lines, dashed centerlines, reversals into a left turn lane, left edge lines, two-way left turn lanes, and lead-in and lead-out patterns. RPMs are placed at least 150 mm (6 in) from any crosswalk or limit line. Marker types shown are Type D two-way yellow reflective and Type G one-way clear reflective, with lead-in spacing of 6.1 m (20 ft) minimum, 7.3 m (24 ft) standard and 9.1 m (30 ft) maximum.
clean.notes:
Note: Raised pavement markers to be installed at a minimum distance of 150 mm (6 in) from any crosswalk line or limit line.

Detail 4: 200 mm (8 in) white right turn lane stripe (through traffic side). Detail 5: White lane line stripe. Detail 6: Dashed centerline. Detail 7: Reversal into left turn lane. Detail 8: Left edge line with single yellow stripe (median side).
Note on Detail 7: 3.6 m (12 ft) striping to be used only in the reversal.
Legend (shown on sheet 2 of 3): Type D 2-way yellow marker is drawn as a square with an X. Type G 1-way clear marker is drawn as a half-filled square. Yellow stripe is a solid line and white stripe is a hatched bar.

Detail 2, painted median: Two parallel solid yellow lines, with a single row of Type D markers on the through traffic side only, spaced 7.3 m (24') and 7.3 m (24'). Stripe width 50 mm (2") TYP.

clean.title: Post Extension and Sign Mounting
clean.summary: Pasadena standard plan S-716 shows how to extend an existing U-channel sign post with a lapped section and how to strap-mount a sign to an existing street light or other pole. Hardware is galvanized steel bolts, a 5 mm spacer with fiber washer, and a stainless steel strap with neoprene-washer bracket. Clearance from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign must be 2.1 m (7 ft).
clean.notes:
Note: Clearance from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign shall be 2.1 m (7').

Callouts: Section as specified 1.0 m (3') or 1.2 m (4'). 205 mm (8") minimum (MIN.). 0.3 m (1') MIN. overlap as needed for sign height. 5 mm (1/8") spacer with fiber washer, 2 each (EA.) sign. Galvanized steel 8 mm (5/16") button head bolt and square nut. Galvanized steel 8 mm (5/16") square head bolt, square washer. Galvanized steel strapped-on bracket with 8 mm (5/16") tapped hole, stainless steel bracket, and neoprene washer. 16 mm x 0.75 mm (5/8" x 0.03") stainless steel strap.
clean.description:
Sheet S-716, City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department standard plan, revision 1, units DUAL (metric with US customary in parentheses), sheet 1 of 1, dated 7-23-01. It has two isometric details, a U-channel post extension on the left and a strap mounting on an existing street light or other pole on the right.

U-channel post extension: An existing U-channel post is shown with a short U-channel post section lapped onto it, with a sign mounted on the face of the post. The added section is 1.0 m (3') or 1.2 m (4') long, as specified, and its lower end overlaps the existing post by a minimum of 0.3 m (1'), with overlap as needed for sign height. Bolt holes in the lapped section are spaced at 205 mm (8") minimum between the bolts that join the two posts. Each connection uses a galvanized steel 8 mm (5/16") square head bolt with square washer (the label also shows square nut). The sign is held off the post by a 5 mm (1/8") spacer with fiber washer, 2 each sign, and is attached with galvanized steel 8 mm (5/16") button head bolts and square nuts. Labels: SIGN, EXISTING U-CHANNEL POST. The detail is titled U-CHANNEL POST EXTENSION.

Strap mounting, existing street light or other pole: An isometric view of a round pole with a sign mounted to it using two strapped-on brackets, one near the top and one near the bottom of the sign. Each bracket is a galvanized steel strapped-on bracket with an 8 mm (5/16") tapped hole, a stainless steel strap, and a neoprene washer. The strap is a 16 mm x 0.75 mm (5/8" x 0.03") stainless steel strap with a buckle. A bolt with round washer, shown on a dashed line, passes through the sign into each bracket. Label: SIGN. The detail is titled STRAP MOUNTING, EXISTING STREET LIGHT OR OTHER POLE.

Note at bottom left: clearance from the ground to the bottom of the lowest sign is 2.1 m (7').

clean.title: STOP Sign and Post Replacement
clean.summary: Pasadena standard plan S-717 shows replacement of a 760 mm (30 in) R1R STOP sign on a 3.0 m (10 ft) galvanized square tube post that slips into a 610 mm (24 in) anchor tube set in a concrete-filled hole. The sign bottom is 2.1 m (7 ft) above grade and the tubes are joined with 9.5 mm (3/8 in) drive rivets. Two notes cover backfill or sidewalk at the surface and concrete requirements.
clean.notes:
Notes:
1. Consolidated backfill or concrete sidewalk, slope to drain.
2. Concrete may be premixed, sacked concrete or field proportioned cement and aggregate with water added and mixing occurring on the job site. 2% calcium chloride (by weight of cement) may be added to produce a quickset concrete. Concrete shall comply with "Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction," latest edition.

Callouts: 760 mm (30") high intensity R1R. 11 mm (7/16") hole, 9.5 mm (3/8") rivet. Galvanized 65 mm (2 1/2") O.D. square tube (12 gauge), 3.0 m (10') long, ASTM-A446. Galvanized 75 mm (3") O.D. square anchor tube [wall thickness 5 mm (3/16")], 610 mm (24") long, ASTM-A500 Grade B. 11 mm (7/16") dia. hole in each tube for 9.5 mm (3/8") drive rivet. Plug end of anchor tube to exclude concrete. Tamped backfill (typical).
clean.description:
Sheet S-717, City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department standard plan, revision 1, units DUAL, sheet 1 of 1, dated 7-23-01. One main elevation with an enlarged detail and Section A-A.

Elevation: A 760 mm (2'-6") high intensity R1R STOP sign (octagon) is mounted on a galvanized 65 mm (2 1/2") O.D. square tube (12 gauge), 3.0 m (10') long, ASTM-A446. The tube top extends 50 mm (2") above the top of the sign. Two rivet points are shown on the post centerline, one near the top and one near the bottom of the sign, each located 75 mm (3") from the sign edge. The bottom of the sign is 2.1 m (7') above the ground line. The post slides into a galvanized 75 mm (3") O.D. square anchor tube [wall thickness 5 mm (3/16")], 610 mm (24") long, ASTM-A500 Grade B. A 1.0 m (3') dimension runs horizontally from the post to the back of the adjacent curb and sidewalk shown at left. The curb section drawn at left shows a depth of 560 mm (1'-10") below grade, with a 50 mm (2") dimension at the base of the sidewalk. Note 1 marks the surface at the post, with a sloped concrete sidewalk edge.

Ground detail: The anchor tube is set in a concrete-filled hole. The hole is 305 mm (12") minimum to 455 mm (18") maximum wide, surrounded by tamped backfill (typical). Concrete (note 2) fills the hole. The anchor tube extends 510 mm (20") minimum to 610 mm (24") maximum below grade and its end is plugged to exclude concrete. A 100 mm (4") dimension shows the top of the anchor tube above grade, with a SLOPE symbol on the sidewalk.

Enlarged detail (circle): The sign post (cut away to show a wavy section) enters the top of the anchor tube. The post projects 25 mm (1") above the top of the anchor tube in the drawn view. Two holes are on adjacent faces of the anchor tube, 50 mm (2") below its top, and the anchor tube is shown with a 150 mm (6") dimension. Label: 11 mm (7/16") dia. hole in each tube for 9.5 mm (3/8") drive rivet.

Section A-A: A plan cut through the sign and post showing the square tube wall with a flat sign face against it, joined by an 11 mm (7/16") hole with a 9.5 mm (3/8") rivet.

clean.title: STOP Sign Post Extension for Street Name Signs Installation
clean.summary: Pasadena standard plan S-718 shows a 57 mm (2 1/4 in) galvanized square steel tube extension, 610 mm (24 in) long, inserted into an existing STOP sign post and fastened with 9.5 mm (3/8 in) drive rivets. Salvaged street name signs and brackets are remounted on it using new stainless steel straps and buckles.
clean.notes:
No numbered notes on this sheet.

Callouts: 57 mm (2 1/4") O.D. square steel tube extension, wall thickness of 12 gauge [3 mm (0.118")], galvanized. 11 mm (7/16") diam. holes for 9.5 mm (3/8") drive rivets (typical (TYP.)): 4 places - post, 3 places - extension. Existing mounting holes on STOP sign post. Salvaged street name signs and brackets (typical). New stainless steel strap and buckle (15 mm x 0.75 mm) (5/8" x 0.03"). Tube extension or street light standard.
clean.description:
Sheet S-718, City of Pasadena Public Works and Transportation Department standard plan, revision 1, units DUAL, sheet 1 of 1, dated 7-23-01. Two isometric details: the STOP sign post extension at left and the street name signs mounted on it at right.

Stop sign post extension (for street name signs): A 57 mm (2 1/4") O.D. square steel tube extension, wall thickness of 12 gauge [3 mm (0.118")], galvanized, is telescoped into the top of the existing STOP sign post. Dimensions: the extension is 610 mm (24") long overall, with 460 mm (18") above the post top and 150 mm (6") inside the post. A 25 mm (1") dimension is shown at the top of the existing post. Rivet holes are spaced 100 mm (4") apart vertically on the post, with a further (4") spacing shown below, and the existing post is drawn with a 610 mm (24") dimension at its lower end. Holes are 11 mm (7/16") diameter for 9.5 mm (3/8") drive rivets (typical): 4 places in the post and 3 places in the extension. The existing mounting holes on the STOP sign post are indicated at the lower end.

Street name signs: An isometric view of the extension tube at the top of the existing post, with two stainless steel straps and buckles wrapped around the post and a street name sign bracket clamped to the face. Salvaged street name signs and brackets (typical) project to the side, with a break line showing the sign blades are longer than drawn. Labels: new stainless steel strap and buckle (15 mm x 0.75 mm) (5/8" x 0.03"), tube extension or street light standard, salvaged street name signs and brackets (typical).
